points.description: Setup and competition: the weights are initialised (randomly, arranged in the lattice topology), an input is sampled from the input space, and similarity matching finds the winning neuron (the neuron whose weight vector is closest to the input). Equivalent wording, or an equivalent distance measure, earns the mark.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.5 if the student gives the winner search without initialisation, or initialisation without a winner search.

points.description: Adaptation and iteration: the winning neuron and its neighbours on the lattice are updated using a neighbourhood function. The neighbourhood size and learning rate are reduced over time, and the process repeats (sampling again) until ordering and convergence are reached. Equivalent wording earns the mark.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.5 if the student updates the winner and neighbours but omits the decay of the neighbourhood/learning rate or the repeat-until-convergence loop.

rubric.notes: Full marks go to pseudocode that initialises the lattice weights, samples an input, finds the best-matching (winning) neuron, updates the winner and its neighbours, shrinks the neighbourhood and learning rate, and repeats until convergence. Half marks go to answers that cover only one half of the procedure (matching without updating, or updating without decay or iteration). No marks go to answers that describe a different algorithm or give no SOM steps.
